approach: Add `PlanEntry::fix` (serde-skipped when false) and change the one sort in `Plan::build_with` (plan.rs:783) from `(e.rung, age)` to `(!e.fix, e.rung, age)`. That sort sees only the dependency-free ready items of the best effective priority (plan.rs:767-782), so the flag cannot beat priority, the urgent and high caps or dependencies. `build_capped` and `build_improving` call `build_with`, so `athena plan` and `athena drain` get the rule from that one key. The flag comes from what the records link, by one function, `hestia::fix_requests_of(records, is_website)`: (a) the open steward-channel requests (`steward::improvement_requests`) unless the request is website or study content, (b) Hestia's waiting root-cause requests (keys of `improvement_of(..).cause_jobs`), (c) waiting requests holding a `Gate under review: NAME.` line. The website test is `reading::is_website_request(text, path_exists)`. It ignores slash-words that are not repository paths (`and/or`, URLs), needs a named website source path, and counts as a fix any request that also names a path that exists at the base commit outside the website sources. `is_website` is passed in as a closure, so hestia.rs stays free of git. `drain.rs` builds the fix set in one private method, `RealSteps::fix_set`, used by `queue()` and `plan_entry()`, and sets `entry.fix` in `entry_of`. Revision by finding: 1 and 2 the two files kept with their reason (hestia.rs, main.rs); 3 and 4 README.md and roles-and-ladder.md dropped; 5 the guard is rebuilt on the base-commit lookup, URLs and non-paths are ignored, and the records-only case is argued to stay a fix; 6 the risk and D181 now say gate-review requests have no guaranteed turn; 7 a cli test ties WEBSITE_PATHS to OUTCOME_PATHS and both doc comments name the difference; 8 lookups happen only for requests that name a website path, and the per-call cost is stated; 9 the demonstration text is corrected.

decisions.choice: Put the fix flag first in the `build_with` sort key, `(!e.fix, e.rung, age)`, after the best-effective-priority filter.
decisions.reason: Root cause of the starvation: inside a tier the order is rung then age (plan.rs:783), and nothing ranks a request that fixes Athena above feature work. The ready set is already cut to dependency-free items (plan.rs:767-775) of the best effective priority (plan.rs:780-781), so priority, the urgent and high caps and dependencies cannot be overridden. `priority_violations` compares priority only (plan.rs:633), so it stays correct. Every caller of `build_with` gets the rule.

rejected.option: Raise fix requests one priority tier in memory, as `build_improving` does for repeated causes (plan.rs:907-919).
rejected.why: It would beat person-set urgent and high work and use the capped urgent and high slots. Changing priority levels or caps is out of scope.

rejected.option: Re-prioritise individual items, or rely on the guaranteed turn (IMPROVEMENT_GAP = 2, plan.rs:466).
rejected.why: The turn moves one request in three; the comment at plan.rs:877 records 5 of 32 steward requests running. The brief asks for the sort key to change.

decisions.choice: Classify by channel and typed links in `hestia::fix_requests_of(records, is_website)`. An open steward-channel request (`steward::improvement_requests`, steward.rs:376-390) is a fix unless `is_website(text)`. Hestia's waiting root-cause requests (keys of `improvement_of(..).cause_jobs`, hestia.rs:977-988) and waiting requests holding a `Gate under review: NAME.` line (GATE_LINE, hestia.rs:1079; open_gate_request, hestia.rs:1140-1147) are fixes too. `is_website` is a closure argument. No key or title match and no work-item lookup.
decisions.reason: `RequestQueue::apply` is the only writer of channel `steward` (steward.rs:662-683) and `decide` applies every item the steward may change as such a request, whatever its kind (steward.rs:710-714), so the channel identifies the steward's requests whether the item is a blind spot, a repeated failure or a Proposal. Hestia files its requests on channel `cli`, so for Hestia the plan uses what the records link, as hestia.rs:957-958 requires. The steward half reuses `improvement_requests`, so the fix set and the guaranteed turn agree on which steward requests are open; an interrupted (dispatched) steward job is in neither and keeps its age place. Passing the website test as a closure keeps hestia.rs free of git and lets the caller supply the base-commit lookup.

rejected.option: Look up steward work items (kind BlindSpot or RepeatedFailure, last job evidence).
rejected.why: The steward's model items other than RepeatedFailure are recorded as Proposal (steward.rs:1045-1048), so most would not be ranked; an approved item is always a Proposal and a person-channel job (work_decisions.rs:51-63, 107-109).

rejected.option: Match 'root cause' or 'gate' in a key or title, as the accepted reading allowed.
rejected.why: A person's request with a similar title would jump the queue and a reworded steward title would drop out; hestia.rs:957 says never by title.

rejected.option: Flag every steward-channel request with no guard.
rejected.why: The owner says the steward's website and study content requests are not fixes.

rejected.option: Also flag the throughput design request and the spec-review requests that `improvement_of` lists.
rejected.why: The owner names root-cause, repeated-failure, blind-spot and gate-review requests only. Those two keep their guaranteed turn; one more line in `fix_requests_of` adds them if the owner wants it.

decisions.choice: Finding 5 and 7: `is_website_request(text, path_exists)` in topics.rs. Take `request_text_touches(text)` (topics.rs:331-342) and drop every word containing `://`. A word is a website path when it starts with an entry of `WEBSITE_PATHS = ["studies/", "xtask/src/site.rs", "xtask/src/decisions.rs", "xtask/tests/site_page.rs", "xtask/tests/fixtures/", ".github/workflows/pages.yml"]`. The request is website content when at least one word is a website path and no other remaining word satisfies `path_exists`. If no word is a website path the function returns false without any lookup. A word that is neither a website path nor an existing path (`and/or`, `pass/fail`, a bare `plan.rs`) is ignored.
decisions.reason: `looks_like_path` accepts any word with a `/` or a known extension (topics.rs:63-72) and `request_text_touches` reads the whole text, so ordinary slash-words and page URLs would otherwise make a website request a fix. The base-commit lookup is what `entry_of` already uses (drain.rs:4354). Every sentence of the page comes from `studies/` and is rendered by `xtask/src/site.rs` and `decisions.rs`; the rest of `xtask/` (`shard.rs`, `ci_cache.rs`, `walltime.rs`, `main.rs`) is Athena's CI tooling and stays a fix. The guard reads the request's own text, which never changes, so the flag is the same before and after a read (topics.rs:397-413 replaces `touches` with the reading's deliverables). Lookups run only for requests that already name a website path, and stop at the first existing path, so ordinary steward requests cost no git calls. `WEBSITE_PATHS` is narrower than `drain::OUTCOME_PATHS` (drain.rs:478: `studies/`, `xtask/`, `pages.yml`) on purpose, because `OUTCOME_PATHS` asks whether a landing can change the page and so takes all of `xtask/`. Both doc comments say so. A cli test asserts every `WEBSITE_PATHS` entry starts with an `OUTCOME_PATHS` prefix, and a core test asserts every `WEBSITE_PATHS` entry exists, so neither list can drift silently.

rejected.option: Reuse `OUTCOME_PATHS` as the website set.
rejected.why: It lives in the cli crate and takes all of `xtask/`, which would demote steward fixes to Athena's CI tooling.

rejected.option: Count every non-website word as a code path.
rejected.why: `and/or`, `pass/fail` and URLs would make website requests fixes, which is the leak the critic found.

rejected.option: Count a non-existent path outside the website sources as code.
rejected.why: It cannot be told from `and/or`. Limit, stated in D181: a request naming a studies path and only a new, not yet existing file elsewhere counts as website.

rejected.option: Guard on `entry.touches`.
rejected.why: It flips to the reading's deliverables after a read, so the same item would rank differently before and after.

decisions.choice: A request whose only named path is the `records/` source fallback (steward.rs:626-633) stays a fix, and the plan does not add a rule for it. A table case in the topics.rs and hestia.rs tests pins this.
decisions.reason: The steward's sources are the records, events, introspections, failure classes, decisions, the git log and the code (steward.rs:174-206); none is the page or studies. `blind_spot_change` files its request with the source path as the file (steward.rs:754-764), so a records-only `Files:` line is the signature of the blind-spot and repeated-failure requests the owner wants first. Nothing in the text of a request with no website path marks it as website content. Treating records-only requests as non-fixes would unrank the main class the owner names. A website request that names a `studies/` or generator path is covered. A website request that names no path at all cannot be identified, and D181 states that limit.

rejected.option: Treat a request with only `records/` paths as website content.
rejected.why: It would unrank the steward's blind-spot requests, the class the owner asks to rank first.

rejected.option: Match words such as 'page' or 'explainer' in the text.
rejected.why: A text match on free words is the title-match the plan rejects for the same reason, and the steward never reads the page.

decisions.choice: Compute the fix set in one private method `RealSteps::fix_set(records, head)` and call it once per `queue()` and once per `plan_entry()`. `entry_of` takes `fixes: &BTreeSet<String>` and sets `entry.fix = fixes.contains(job)`. `reading::plan_entry` stays free of records and leaves `fix` false.
decisions.reason: `entry_of` runs once per queued item (drain.rs:4527-4530), so the set is built once per `queue()`, not per item. `plan_entry` is also the entry that replaces the queue entry after a read (drain.rs:2282), so it must set the flag too, or a read would drop it. One method owns the rule. Cost per `plan_entry` call (finding 8): the call is made by the read pass for each underspecified request (drain.rs:2282), by `vet` for each read-ahead job (drain.rs:2078, touches only), and for approved proposals (drain.rs:3104). Each call already loads all records (drain.rs:4544 `self.records()`) and makes a git lookup per touched path. `fix_set` adds one scan of jobs and introspections held in memory (the same scan `RealSteps::improvement` makes on every re-plan, drain.rs:4568-4572) and no git calls for requests that name no website path. It is not measured; the producer should not add caching unless a test run shows a slowdown.

rejected.option: Leave `plan_entry` flag-free and copy the queue entry's flag after a read.
rejected.why: It adds a hidden contract between the read pass and the queue and needs a stub Steps test to cover it; recomputing is simpler and self-consistent.

rejected.option: Compute the flag inside `entry_of` for each job.
rejected.why: It repeats the records scan for every queued item.

rejected.option: Set the steward half inside `reading::plan_entry` from the job's channel.
rejected.why: It splits one rule over two places; the Hestia half needs the records.

decisions.choice: Cap slots follow the plan order, so inside a full tier a fix request keeps its slot ahead of an older feature request. Person-set priorities are still counted first and never demoted. The consequence is stated in D181, the CHANGELOG entry and the `athena drain --help` text, and tested.
decisions.reason: `build_capped` hands out slots in the uncapped plan order (plan.rs:811-818, 847-865) and its doc says the others keep slots in the plan's own order (plan.rs:801-802). The fix flag is now part of that order. Hestia's root-cause requests are queued High (hestia.rs:1012-1014), so a non-person high feature request can be demoted to normal in favour of one. The cap values do not change, only which item holds a slot.

rejected.option: Compute slots from an order with the flag cleared.
rejected.why: A second build and a second ordering rule for a case the owner did not ask about.

decisions.choice: Findings 1 to 4: keep hestia.rs and main.rs, drop README.md and docs/design/roles-and-ladder.md. hestia.rs gets `fix_requests_of` and a private `has_gate_line` beside the private `GATE_LINE`. main.rs gets the `athena drain --help` Order text.
decisions.reason: hestia.rs: GATE_LINE is private (hestia.rs:1079) and hestia.rs:957-958 owns the rule that requests are found by what the records link; a copy of the literal in a listed file would give one marker two definitions, and the owner names gate-review requests. If the host refuses the file, the fallback is to drop the gate-review half and put the steward half and `improvement_of(..).cause_jobs` in drain.rs (both public); D181 would say so. main.rs: the help's Order text says 'then higher rung, then age as the tiebreak' (main.rs:302-304) and would become false; D156 (decisions.md:4271-4273) records a job rejected because its change left that help false. README.md:145-148 and roles-and-ladder.md:73-74 are coarse summaries that already omit priority and the guaranteed turn; they are left unchanged like docs/ontology.toml:31, and D181 names all three. No test pins their wording.

rejected.option: Edit README.md and roles-and-ladder.md as well.
rejected.why: Two more files outside the deliverables for summaries that were already incomplete.

rejected.option: Match the gate literal in drain.rs.
rejected.why: It duplicates a private marker with nothing tying the copy to the original.

rejected.option: Leave the help text unchanged.
rejected.why: A known-false order sentence in the help is the failure D156 describes.

decisions.choice: Gate-review requests are ranked as fixes but get no guaranteed turn. The plan does not add them to `improvement_of`.
decisions.reason: `improvement_of` (hestia.rs:973-1007) lists steward requests, repeated-cause requests, throughput design requests and spec requests and never reads `Gate under review:` lines, so the fix set is wider than the improvement set by exactly the gate requests. Changing the guaranteed turn is outside the request. D181, the CHANGELOG and the risks say so.

rejected.option: Add gate requests to `improvement_of` so both sets agree.
rejected.why: It changes how many requests get a guaranteed turn, which the owner did not ask for.

decisions.choice: The accepted reading's 'approved work item' route is not built. A work item the steward applies is a queued request on the steward channel; an approved item is always a Proposal and its job is a person-channel job.
decisions.reason: `find_open` refuses any kind other than Proposal (work_decisions.rs:107-109) and `open_proposals` lists only Proposals (work_decisions.rs:51-63), so an approved item is never a BlindSpot or RepeatedFailure. `approve_work` submits the job through `ask` (work_decisions.rs:344-345), channel `cli` (reading.rs:955). An approved owner-bound proposal keeps its place by rung and age; D181 states it.

rejected.option: Flag jobs that carry out an approved steward proposal.
rejected.why: They are owner-bound environment or token requests, not the fixes the owner lists.

risks.risk: Every open steward request that is not website content now ranks ahead of same-priority person requests, so normal feature work can wait behind a long run of steward requests. This is the goal the owner set but it moves the starvation to the other side.
risks.mitigation: A person's `athena priority <job> <level>` record or urgent/high words still decide before the flag, and the guaranteed turn is unchanged. The help text, D181 and the CHANGELOG say plainly that feature work of the same tier waits for ready fix requests.

risks.risk: How many of the 52 requests the rule ranks is not known: the records are absent from the snapshot, and the website guard removes the ones whose text names a website source path.
risks.mitigation: D181 and the CHANGELOG say the share was not measured. The tests show the guard on each side of the line.

risks.risk: The website guard is a hard-coded list plus a base-commit lookup. A renamed file drops out of the list. A website request that names no path (or only the `records/` fallback) cannot be identified and counts as a fix. A request naming a studies path and only a new, not yet existing file elsewhere counts as website. Page text hard-coded in `xtask/src/site.rs` cannot be told from generator logic by path.
risks.mitigation: A unit test checks every listed path exists, and a cli test ties the list to `OUTCOME_PATHS`. The records-only case is a fix on purpose: the steward's blind-spot requests use that fallback (steward.rs:754-764). D181 states each limit.

risks.risk: A person's request that cites a repeated cause's introspection ids or holds a `Gate under review:` line also counts as a fix, because hestia.rs:967-968 links by what a request cites, not who wrote it.
risks.mitigation: D181 states it. The repeated-cause half matches the guaranteed-turn rule. The gate half does not: `improvement_of` never reads gate lines (hestia.rs:973-1007), so gate-review requests are ranked as fixes but get no guaranteed turn. D181 and the CHANGELOG say so.

risks.risk: A non-person high feature request can lose a cap slot to a high fix request (Hestia's root-cause requests are queued High, hestia.rs:1012-1014) and be demoted to normal sooner than before. This sits near the out-of-scope 'caps' item.
risks.mitigation: The cap values and demotion rules are unchanged; person-set items are counted first and never demoted. The consequence is chosen, tested, and written in the help text, the CHANGELOG entry and D181.

risks.risk: Two files outside the listed deliverables change (hestia.rs and main.rs), which widens the scope. README.md and roles-and-ladder.md are not edited and keep a coarse order summary.
risks.mitigation: Each change is small, has a stated reason in decision 7 and is not a governance file. If the host refuses hestia.rs, the fallback is to compute the steward half and the root-cause half in drain.rs from the public `steward::improvement_requests` and `improvement_of(..).cause_jobs`, drop the gate-review half, and say so in D181.

risks.risk: Cost per call: `fix_set` runs on every `queue()` and `plan_entry()` call, which the read pass and `vet` make once per item. It runs `improvement_of`, which scans introspections.
risks.mitigation: Each call already loads all records and makes a git lookup per touched path, so the scan is small beside it (estimate, not measured). Requests that name no website path need no git calls in the website test, and a website request stops at its first existing path. The producer adds no cache unless a test run shows a slowdown.

risks.risk: The criterion 3 and 4 fixtures could leave a request without a rung (which refuses it), give requests different rungs so age no longer decides, or queue two requests in the same clock tick so the age tie breaks by random job id.
risks.mitigation: Each steward request is built through `StewardRequest`, which always writes an acceptance bullet and a `Files:` line (steward.rs:535-595) and names a path, so `infer_rung` gives Implementation without a read (topics.rs:256-259). The tests assert equal rungs, that every item is in `plan.order`, none refused, and the `received_at` order of the queued requests, before they assert the plan order.

risks.risk: The new D181, CHANGELOG and help text, or the test texts, could trip the boundary-word scan or name a person or the live page address.
risks.mitigation: The text calls the requester 'the owner' and names no person, machine or email; the test texts use `https://example.com/page`. `cargo test --locked` runs the policy scan.

demonstrations.method: Unit test `a_ready_fix_entry_comes_before_an_older_feature_entry_of_the_same_tier` in `mod tests` of crates/athena-core/src/plan.rs. Entries come from the existing `entry(id, rung, touches, deps)` helper (plan.rs:1159): an older normal entry `feature` first in the slice, then a newer normal entry `fix` with `fix = true`. It calls `Plan::build_with` and `Plan::build_improving` with `TierCaps::UNLIMITED`, an empty `person_set` and `Improvement::default()` (the call `athena plan` and `athena drain` make). It runs the same two entries with `fix` false as a control, and a case where the fix entry has the lower rung (Implementation against BriefRequirements), so rung order cannot be what put it first.
demonstrations.observes: `plan.order == ["fix", "feature"]` from both builders, including with the fix entry on the lower rung. The control with `fix` false gives `["feature", "fix"]`.
demonstrations.fails_without: With the sort key left at `(e.rung, *age)` the newer fix entry stays behind the older feature entry, so the `plan.order` assertion fails and the flagged run would not differ from the control.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points `Plan::build_with` (plan.rs:692) and `Plan::build_improving` (plan.rs:894) exist. The fixture is plain `PlanEntry` data from the existing `entry` helper; nothing is doubled. The `fix` field and the new key are added by plan steps 1 and 2.

demonstrations.method: Two unit tests in plan.rs `mod tests`. (1) `the_fix_flag_never_overrides_priority_or_dependencies`, through `Plan::build_with` with `with_priority` (plan.rs:1662): (a) an older urgent feature, an older high feature and a newer normal fix; (b) a normal fix that depends on a newer normal non-fix with a lower rung; (c) a normal non-fix that is a dependency of a high feature, beside a normal fix; (d) two fix and two feature entries in one tier with different rungs and ages. (2) `the_fix_flag_decides_a_full_tier_slot_in_plan_order`, through `Plan::build_capped` with `TierCaps { urgent: 3, high: 1 }`: an older high feature `f` and a newer high fix `x`, first with an empty `person_set`, then with `person_set = ["f"]`.
demonstrations.observes: (a) order urgent, high, fix. (b) the prerequisite comes before the fix entry that needs it. (c) the prerequisite is raised to high by `effective_priorities` (plan.rs:758) and comes before the normal fix. (d) both fix entries, then both feature entries, each pair by rung then age. Test two with an empty person set: `plan.order == ["x", "f"]`, `plan.demoted` holds one entry for `f` (High to Normal, cap 1) and the capped copy of `x` is still High. With `f` in `person_set`: `f` keeps the slot, `x` is demoted and the order is `["f", "x"]`.
demonstrations.fails_without: A key that put the flag above effective priority, or sorted before the best-tier filter, puts the normal fix ahead of the urgent and high features in (a) and ahead of the raised prerequisite in (c). A key that ignored `depends_on` puts the dependent fix first in (b). Without the flag in the order, test two's `x` would not take the slot and `f` would not be demoted. Each fails an order or demotion assertion.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points `Plan::build_with` (plan.rs:692) and `Plan::build_capped` (plan.rs:804) exist. Fixtures are `PlanEntry` values with `priority`, `depends_on` and `fix` set through the existing `entry` and `with_priority` helpers. The `fix` field is added by plan step 1. Nothing is doubled.

It queues one older person feature request with `athena.queue(&complete_request("crates/f/lib.rs", ""))` (tests/drain.rs:6319), then three steward-channel requests and one more, with `queue_steward_request` (tests/drain.rs:2573, through `RequestQueue::apply` as the steward does), oldest to newest: `studies` (title and body mention `pass/fail`, `and/or` and `https://example.com/page`; the one file is `studies/demo/intro.json`), `site` (only `xtask/src/site.rs`), `tooling` (only `xtask/src/shard.rs`), `mixed` (`studies/demo/intro.json` and `src/lib.rs`, which exists at the fixture head). That is one person request plus four steward requests. It calls `drain::plan(&Replay::new(real_steps(..), None), 5.0, &Quiet)` and reads `PlanReport::entries` (oldest first, drain.rs:3436-3438) and `plan.order`. It also calls `RealSteps::plan_entry(job)` for each steward request, the path the read pass takes. Supporting tests: `cargo test -p athena-core is_website_request` (the table in topics.rs: studies only true; studies with `and/or`, `pass/fail` and a URL true; studies plus an existing `crates/` path false; studies plus a non-existent new file elsewhere true, the stated limit; no path false; URL only false; `records/` only false; `xtask/src/site.rs` true; existing `xtask/src/shard.rs` false; pages.yml true; existing `.github/workflows/ci.yml` false; `studies-extra/x.json` false; every `WEBSITE_PATHS` entry exists), `cargo test -p athena-core fix_requests_of` (the hestia.rs test), and `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain website_paths_are_outcome_paths` (every `WEBSITE_PATHS` entry starts with an `OUTCOME_PATHS` prefix).
demonstrations.observes: All entries have rung Some(Implementation), checked first so age and not rung decides, and none is in `plan.refused`. The queue order is asserted from each request's `received_at` first, so a clock tie is a loud precondition failure. `plan.order == [tooling, mixed, feature, studies, site]`. `studies` and `site` have `fix == false`; `tooling` and `mixed` have `fix == true`; `RealSteps::plan_entry` returns the same flags for the four steward requests.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the classifier flagged every steward-channel request, `studies` and `site` would move ahead of the older feature request and the order and `fix == false` assertions fail. If it flagged nothing, `tooling` would stay behind the feature and the order fails. If slash-words and URLs counted as paths, `studies` would be a fix and fail. If an existing non-website path did not make a request a fix, `mixed` would stay last and fail. If the flag were set only in `queue()` and not in `plan_entry()`, the `plan_entry` assertion fails.
